question.problem:
Consider two sets of $28$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{28},$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{28}.$ You are given that

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\sum }_{i=1}^{28}{x}_{i}=560,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{28}{y}_{i}=588, \\  & {\sum }_{i=1}^{28}{x}_{i}^{2}=10\,920,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{28}{y}_{i}^{2}=13\,220.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the sum of the squared deviations from the mean for the points ${y}_{i}.$

${S}_{yy}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n},$ the sum of squared deviations from the mean for the data ${y}_{i}$ can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{yy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y})^{2} \\  & ={\sum }_{i}{y}_{i}^{2}-\frac{1}{n}{({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the given statistics in the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{yy} & =13\,220-\frac{1}{28}(588)^{2} \\  & =13\,220-12\,348 \\  & =872.\end{aligned}
$$
